This was the time of Jalal Al-e Ahmad’s virulent
criticism of gharbzadegi (“Westoxication,” alternatively
translated as “Weststruckness” or “Occidentosis”)
in 1962.47 Gharbzadegi refers to the uncritical and
pathological infatuation of secular nationalists
with things European; this infatuation had, in Ale-e
Ahmad’s view and that of other intellectuals, gradually
replaced “backwardness” (as Iran’s main sociohistorical
problem) with alienation.48 According to Boroujerdi,
